title: Hom complex from a K-flat into a K-injective complex is K-injective
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal L^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] and $\mathcal I^\bullet$ a K-injective complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then the Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is K-injective.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal K^\bullet$ be any acyclic complex of $\mathcal O$-modules. By the definition of K-flatness, the total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal L^\bullet)$ is acyclic.

By [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] (applied with $\mathcal M^\bullet=\mathcal I^\bullet$) there is an isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet))\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal L^\bullet),\mathcal I^\bullet)$.

source.place: Lemma 0A96 (lemma-compose), tensor-Hom calculation in the proof

proof.text: For the acyclic total tensor complex from Step 1, K-injectivity of $\mathcal I^\bullet$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal L^\bullet),\mathcal I^\bullet)=0$. For complexes $\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal B^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules, the global sections $\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal B^\bullet))$ form the complex whose degree-$n$ terms are families of $\mathcal O$-linear maps $\mathcal A^p\to\mathcal B^{p+n}$ with the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex]; its degree-zero cocycles are the morphisms of complexes and its degree-zero coboundaries are exactly the null-homotopic ones, so $H^0(\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal B^\bullet)))=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal B^\bullet)$. Taking global sections and $H^0$ of the isomorphism of Step 2 therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet))=0$ for every acyclic $\mathcal K^\bullet$. By the definition of K-injectivity, $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ is K-injective.
